transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Start: 15:00 UTC (00:00)
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Leah (CSM), Ethan (SE) -- Meridian: Sofia, Ravi, Maya, Tom

Summary (auto): QBR / ongoing health check focusing on usage trends, recent cost spike, reliability incidents in Nov, and roadmap alignment for Dedicated pilot in Jan. Agreed next steps include cost breakdown, perf benchmarks, and a technical deep dive on caching/kv eviction.

Topics: usage & cost, latency/reliability, security/compliance check, Dedicated pilot sizing, roadmap dates

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. we'll do a quick QBR style health check, go over usage, costs, reliability items, and then talk about next steps for the Dedicated pilot. Sofia, do you want to kick us off with a quick summary of what's changed on your side?

[00:28] Sofia: Yeah thanks Jordan, um hi all. We've seen steady increase in queries from the merch assistants—i mean, the recommender microservice—so traffic is up about 42% month-over-month. Most of the extra volume is mid-day peak, which is where we've been hitting higher token costs. we also had two incidents in early Nov where latency spiked and some requests timed out, so we routed to fallback models.

[01:10] Leah: Thanks for that. Jordan, do you want to run through the usage graphs? I know we shared a quick snapshot before the call.

[01:18] Jordan: Sure, quick share. So high level: total tokens up ~45% YoY, 42% MoM this quarter; embedding requests are flat, generation calls are the driver. The billing run for November shows an overage relative to the committed plan — Tom I think you flagged that with us?

[01:45] Tom: Yeah, Tom here. We saw the invoice and the spike was unexpected. We were hoping the batching suggestions would keep it lower. We need a clearer explanation of what happened and what the easy wins are.

[02:05] Ethan: One immediate thing we noticed is that prefix caching wasn't enabled on a few routes. Also some of the prompt construction at Meridian is duplicating system instructions in each call, so there are redundant tokens. If we apply batching and prefix caching we'll see token cost drop 20-35% depending on the workload.

[02:35] Ravi: On the platform side, our app does micro-bursting—lots of small requests with ~8-12 tokens each. Batching sounds good but some of our endpoints are latency sensitive, we can't add a 50 ms wait for batching unless P95 stays under 120 ms.

[03:05] Ethan: Understood. We can tune batching windows and use smart routing so sensitive endpoints go to low-latency pools. Also the Dedicated cluster gives more consistent P95 since it's reserved capacity.

[03:28] Sofia: About the incidents—what's Redwood's view on what caused the timeouts? Was it autoscaling lag, or model OOMs?

[03:40] Jordan: We did an internal postmortem on that. It was a combination: a sudden spike + a kernel mismatch on one host causing a degraded node, and autoscaler took a few minutes to spin up replacement. We had fallback policies that redirected to a smaller model to preserve throughput, but latency degraded.

[04:02] Leah: We've since applied a pre-warm policy on the pool and adjusted autoscaler thresholds for similar patterns. Also we're pushing a runtime fix that reduces kernel selection variance, ETA early Jan.

[04:20] Maya: For our execs it's about predictability. They want a guaranteed latency SLA during peak hours or at least predictable costs. How does Dedicated pricing and SLAs look?

[04:35] Jordan: Dedicated comes with a predictable throughput contract. You commit to a pool size, we guarantee latency targets for that pool, and we provide a monthly commit. There's also burst capacity add-ons. I can share a draft contract and pricing that maps to your expected QPS.

[04:50] Tom: And what about data security? We need SOC 2, audit logs, SSO, and KMS integration — all must be audit-ready.

[05:05] Ethan: We support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated deployments. We can share the security pack; for Dedicated we can also enable VPC peering and customer access to audit logs.

[05:30] Sofia: Great, please include retention windows and log formats. We may need 13 months retention for certain logs.

[05:40] Jordan: Noted. We'll add retention details.

[05:50] -- Transcript moves into technical specifics --

[06:10] Ethan: Quick perf note: if you enable prefix caching on the recommendation service, you can reuse KV cache across requests for the same session which eliminates repeated attention computation. On your sample, we saw ~30% CPU savings and P95 improved by ~18 ms. But cache sizing matters — need to know retention window and hit rate expectations.

[06:45] Ravi: We're targeting a 10 minute conversation window on KV cache and 80% hit rate at peak, but our team needs guidance on eviction policy and memory sizing.

[07:05] Ethan: For that hit rate you'd want a cache size roughly equivalent to the working set of unique prefixes — we can help run a profiler. Also quantized model variants reduce memory but increase compute slightly; it's a tradeoff.

[07:25] Sofia: On the roadmap side, what Redwood changes are coming Q1 that we should know about?

[07:32] Leah: Quick bullets: 1) runtime kernel improvements for better P99 behavior (early Jan), 2) improved automatic batching heuristics (late Jan), 3) extended KV cache controls including TTL-based eviction, and 4) a Dedicated onboarding playbook. We'll share dates and docs.

[07:55] Maya: Any changes to billing model or metering we should expect with those features?

[08:05] Jordan: No fundamental metering changes; we're introducing better cost allocation exports and token-level breakdowns per route in the console — that should land mid-Jan. That will help the finance team reconcile.

[08:20] Tom: That's helpful. We want per-route cost visibility and ability to attribute to product teams so we can chargeback.

[08:32] Jordan: We'll include that in the deck I send.

[08:40] -- 10 minute mark review --

[09:00] Sofia: Also curious about A/B and rollout support. We plan a canary rollout for a new prompt template next sprint. Any tips on how Redwood handles A/B?

[09:14] Ethan: You can use route-level rollouts with percent traffic and automatic fallback. We'll capture evals against your prompt set and provide quality regressions alerts. For the canary we recommend a 5% traffic ramp with automated checks for latency and quality metrics.

[09:40] Ravi: On the Dedicated sizing: we'll provide expected QPS curves but want Redwood's recommendation on GPU type and memory. Can you give a ballpark?

[09:50] Jordan: For your workloads we typically recommend an A100-like capacity for high throughput embeddings and a mixture of H100-equivalent for generation-heavy models. But final recommendation depends on sequence length distributions — the benchmark Ethan will run will nail it down.

[10:10] -- Mid-call: cost deep-dive --

[10:30] Tom: Back to costs: what are the quick wins to lower token consumption without affecting quality?

[10:40] Ethan: 1) remove duplicated system prompts, 2) prefix caching, 3) shared prompts in session context to reduce repeated system token sends, 4) better sampling and temperature settings for lower gen lengths, 5) use quantized model for bulk inference where acceptable. We saw 20-35% savings in similar customers.

[11:05] Sofia: Are there any downsides to quantization for our use case? We care about fidelity for product copy generation.

[11:15] Ethan: Quantization slightly affects generation quality—sometimes subtle. For copy generation we'd suggest evals: run prompts through quantized variant and compare BLEU/style metrics. If it passes, you can move bulk jobs to quantized. We'll help with eval harness.

[11:40] Leah: Also note our Redwood Optimize recommendations will generate model/quantization suggestions based on your historical traces — we'll send those as part of the cost breakdown.

[12:00] -- Reliability / incidents detail --

[12:20] Ravi: For the Nov incident can you share logs or traces showing autoscaler behavior and which nodes were impacted?

[12:28] Jordan: Yes, we'll export the incident trace and autoscaler events. Expect a zipped trace with timestamps and node IDs. We'll redact any internal-only identifiers.

[12:45] Tom: Good. We might need that for our postmortem.

[12:52] Jordan: We'll include it.

[13:05] -- Planning pilot --

[13:20] Jordan: Let's align on pilot scope: Dedicated pilot starting ~2027-01-10, 3 month pilot, objective: validate P95/P99 under your peak load, verify cost predictability, and test KMS + SSO integration. Does that match expectations?

[13:40] Sofia: Yes that matches. We'll confirm internal approval but that's the timeline we prefer.

[13:50] Maya: We'll also want a runbook for failover to hosted during maintenance windows.

[13:58] Ethan: We have a documented canary and fallback playbook; we'll share the playbook and template runbooks.

[14:15] -- Closing recap and next steps --

[14:25] Leah: Quick recap: Jordan will send cost breakdown and per-route token trends; Ethan will run perf benchmarks on sample prompts and advise on cache sizing; Leah will share the Q1 roadmap deck and Dedicated onboarding playbook; Ravi will share expected QPS and retention needs. We'll schedule a technical deep dive for caching the week of Dec 13.

[14:55] Jordan: Anything else?

[15:02] Tom: Just please flag any upcoming maintenance windows that affect latency.

[15:08] Jordan: Will do. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and confirm the pilot start date.

End transcript.
